nieuw.titel: Avoid relying on heavy cavalry to grind ranked blocks
nieuw.tekst: Choose heavy cavalry's targets with its initial charge in mind. Do not expect it to grind through a large ranked block if it fails to break that block on the charge.
nieuw.waarom: He says lance- and cavalry-spear-armed units lose much of their Strength and armour penetration after the charge. In his view, a large ranked block that survives that charge will eventually get the better of them.

nieuw.titel: Use monstrous cavalry for fights that may need grinding
nieuw.tekst: Use monstrous cavalry against targets that may survive the initial charge and require further rounds of fighting. The speaker considers it better suited to this role than traditional heavy cavalry.
nieuw.waarom: He says monstrous cavalry remains durable and continues dealing damage in subsequent rounds, often because its mounts contribute powerful, high-Strength attacks.

nieuw.titel: Use faster regular cavalry to apply earlier pressure
nieuw.tekst: Where regular cavalry is faster than your heavy cavalry option, use that extra reach to threaten earlier and restrict how far opponents feel able to advance.
nieuw.waarom: He says even an extra inch of threat can discourage an enemy advance. Against a gunline, the extra marching distance gets the cavalry up the table sooner and forces earlier decisions, giving the opponent more opportunities to make mistakes.

nieuw.titel: Sacrifice cheaper cavalry to prepare a heavy cavalry breakthrough
nieuw.tekst: Consider sending cheaper regular cavalry into a dangerous enemy to inflict damage before committing your heavy cavalry. Use that damage to help the heavy cavalry break through in subsequent turns.
nieuw.waarom: He says regular cavalry can hit hard enough to damage a dangerous target while costing less than the knights he would be reluctant to commit first.

nieuw.titel: Manoeuvre light missile cavalry into chaff-clearing shooting angles
nieuw.tekst: Use light missile cavalry's mobility to find shooting angles and clear enemy chaff. Treat it as a shooting unit rather than charging it into skirmishers as you might with other light cavalry.
